newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Gazprom agrees to pipe Turkmen gas.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom agrees to pipe Turkmen gas.

text.p: Russia's RAO Gazprom has agreed to supply gas from Turkmenistan to Ukraine and western Europe through Russian pipelines, the official Turkmen-Press news agency said on Monday.

"We have agreed to supply Turkmen gas in 1997," Gazprom chief Rem Vyakhirev said after a meeting with Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov on Friday. "This will be accomplished by sending it two ways -- to Ukraine and Europe," he said, cited by the agency.
Vyakhirev gave no details on export volumes, saying only that they would depend on winter demand for heating and in Ukraine's case, the republic's ability to pay.
Turkmen-Press said Ukraine's plans to pay for gas imports would be known at the end of the month.

In October, Ukrainian Finance Minister Valentyn Koronevsky said the republic, which plans to import around 20 billion cubic metres of gas from Turkmenistan this year, would pay Turkmenistan $194 million in 1997 for gas debts.
But for Turkmenistan's hard-hit economy, exports of gas to western Europe are the most crucial.

Turkmenistan's gas was once exported to Western Europe and is still its main source of export revenue. But Russia has barred pipeline access to the West, leaving Turkmenistan to export its gas to other impoverished former Soviet republics which cannot pay.

The republic, now totally reliant on Russian export pipelines, is building a new one south to neighbouring Iran and there are also plans to build an export pipeline to Pakistan via war-torn Afghanistan.
The desert nation of 3.8 million saw gas production in 1995 sink to 35.6 billion cubic metres from 63.5 billion cubic metres in 1993.
